what: A box is painted with a linear gradient (four colors · 0 · .4 · .7 · 1), and the span between two chosen colors is carved with an 8×8 Bayer threshold (.5) and mixed into two-color dots of 3px (2px on phones). The reveal uses the same threshold: each cell turns on when its share of 2×progress − distance from the start edge exceeds that cell’s threshold, so a band dissolves into dots and fills from one side (.8s cubic in-out). Hook it to one of: on load (load), when 20% enters the screen (enter), or on receiving fx:in/fx:out (event). Give each line a delay and text-line bands open in sequence.

options.on: load (on open) · enter (once when entering the screen) · event (on receiving fx:in/fx:out — detail.dur·detail.delay seconds) · none (fully painted from the start), default load
options.dir: Reveal direction: right (left→right) · left · up (bottom→top) · down, default right
options.angle: Gradient direction (degrees) — 0 is left→right, 90 is top→bottom, 180 is right→left, default 0
options.at: Color slots (space-separated 0~1), default "0 .4 .7 1" — Colors are CSS variables --fx-c0 · --fx-c1 … in the same order
options.dither: Numbers of the two colors to blend per dot, default the last two ("2 3")
options.look: duotone (two-color dots) · overlay (only the front-color dots sit over the gradient), default duotone
options.dot: Dot size (px), default 3 — dot-sm applies below 767px, default 2
options.enter: on: portion that must be visible on enter, default .2
options.--fx-c0 … --fx-c3: Band color (css variable — on the box or an ancestor), default accent → accent → half accent and half text color → the darker one

from.where: index.html .sh-fv .sh-row__band (hero text-line band — original Dithering.js: primary-heading 0·.4·.7·1, dither 2→3 duotone, 8×8 Bayer · 3px (2px below 767) · multiplied by dpr, reveal 800ms easeInOut (cubic) · revealAngle 180 · 60ms per line (40ms on phone)) · .sh-statement background (primary-body 90° · bottom→top 1000ms · 650ms delay · overlay) · ISSUE heading line band (on hover .4s · 30ms per line — fx:in/fx:out)

note: The original is a 2D canvas, so there are no shaders. Even if the gradient angle is not a multiple of 90°, each cell is projected onto the axis and cut at the same threshold
